blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Longitudes are imaginary semi-circles running from the North Pole to the South Pole, converging at the poles.
The Prime Meridian (0° longitude) passes through Greenwich, England, and serves as the baseline for world time zones.
Because the Earth rotates 360° in 24 hours, traveling 15° east or west changes local time by exactly one hour.
The International Date Line roughly follows the 180° meridian; crossing it westward advances the date by one day.
Indian Standard Time (IST) is calculated from 82°30' E longitude, putting India 5 hours and 30 minutes ahead of GMT.
